title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
authors: E. J. W. Koh, Rongjie Zhang, Dzmitry Matsukevich
abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.
summary: This paper reports the experimental realization of an exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate between the motional modes of trapped ions. By combining spin-dependent and spin-independent beam splitter interactions, the authors achieve a continuously tunable gate. The fidelity is verified by measuring the joint characteristic function, demonstrating its utility for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper experimentally implements and characterizes the exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions.
main_result: The measurement of the joint characteristic function confirms the continuous, tunable operation of the eSWAP gate, demonstrating coherent control over the identity-SWAP superposition.
method: The gate is realized using a sequence combining spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions, and the fidelity is measured by analyzing selected slices of the joint characteristic function.
model_or_system: The physical system is trapped ions (specifically using ${}^{171}	ext{Yb}^+$) whose internal spin states interact with their quantized bosonic motional modes. The interactions are modeled using beam splitter Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Joint characteristic function $\chi(\alpha,  eta)$, expectation value of $\langle\hat{\sigma}_zangle$, and the overlap $O_{	ext{exp}}$ between measured and ideal characteristic functions.
important_parameters: The tunable angle $	heta$ of the eSWAP gate, and the measurement relies on characterizing the dependence of $\chi$ on this angle.
main_assumptions: The measurement focuses on selected slices of the joint characteristic function rather than full four-dimensional tomography due to time constraints.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the circuit diagram for the eSWAP gate and show comparisons between measured slices of the joint characteristic function (real and imaginary parts) for various input states against ideal theoretical predictions.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical derivation of the eSWAP gate, outlines the experimental sequence involving beam splitters and spin rotations, and presents the measurement and analysis using the joint characteristic function to verify the gate operation and its tunability.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, high-fidelity platform for implementing complex quantum gates (eSWAP) using motional modes, which is crucial for building scalable quantum processors based on trapped ions.
